analysis:
The only changed file in this batch is CHANGELOG.md. The PR adds documentation entries under 'Unreleased — cache reliability' (patch hunk @@ -210,6 +210,8 @@ and @@ -220,6 +222,11 @@, head lines about 213-228). No executable code, configuration, or trust-boundary logic is visible here.

The entries describe SSD prefix-cache behavior changes that the supplied source does not include:
- Preserving healthy SSD checkpoints during missing-file reconciliation.
- A bounded shorter complete-checkpoint restore after a capacity refusal.
- Rejecting substituted FIFO cache entries while keeping reads and touches unblocked.
- Preserving encrypted SSD checkpoints and routing announcements during routine eviction.
- Coordinating durable writes and index commits with retirement.
- Retrying epoch checks on transient parent-directory open or status probe failures.

Relevant threats are T-041 (cross-tenant prefix cache and SSD offload), A-001 (prompt confidentiality) and TB-007. The changelog states that the encryption, authentication, precision, capture-cap and first-attempt admission behavior is unchanged, and that corrupt or cancelled paths stay cold. These claims are unverified because the implementing code was not supplied.

TB-002 and TB-009 were reviewed as context. Nothing in this diff touches provider attestation, App Attest authorization, WebSocket registration, final handoff, billing, or any other threat-model assertion.

Next-pass focus: if the implementing cache source files are reviewed, check the following.
- Rename-to-index races and epoch fencing, so retiring an entry cannot leave a stale holder or routing announcement.
- Whether a transient failure while disowning records could leave a substituted or unauthenticated checkpoint readable.
- Whether retrying with a shorter checkpoint still authenticates the tenant, key and artifact identity.
- Whether the T-041 mitigation text still matches the new eviction behavior.

This review cannot verify any of those from a changelog-only change.
